module.purpose: Implements the classic `connect` higher-order component for React Redux, binding React components to a Redux store with memoized selectors, subscription management, and ref forwarding.
module.summary: This file provides the `connect` API for react-redux, wrapping a component to inject state and dispatch props derived from a Redux store. It uses internal React hooks (useSyncExternalStore, useMemo, useRef, useLayoutEffect) to manage store subscription, prop selection, and context propagation. It supports custom contexts, forwardRef, and many mapState/mapDispatch/mergeProps combinations via overloaded typings. A deprecation warning is emitted if the removed `pure` option is supplied. The connected component memoizes child elements and coordinates nested subscriptions to avoid unnecessary re-renders.
module.businessContext: React Redux library bridging UI components and Redux state. Critical for legacy connect-based apps; failure breaks component-store binding and UI updates.

detail.name: subscribeUpdates
detail.signature: function subscribeUpdates(shouldHandleStateChanges: boolean, store: Store, subscription: Subscription, childPropsSelector: (state: unknown, props: unknown) => unknown, lastWrapperProps: React.MutableRefObject<unknown>, lastChildProps: React.MutableRefObject<unknown>, renderIsScheduled: React.MutableRefObject<boolean>, isMounted: React.MutableRefObject<boolean>, childPropsFromStoreUpdate: React.MutableRefObject<unknown>, notifyNestedSubs: () => void, additionalSubscribeListener: () => void, displayName: string)
preconditions: All required arguments are provided with the declared types.
When state updates are processed, lastWrapperProps.current, lastChildProps.current, renderIsScheduled.current, isMounted.current, and childPropsFromStoreUpdate.current are available refs.
subscription provides onStateChange, trySubscribe, and tryUnsubscribe operations.
postconditions: If shouldHandleStateChanges is false, no subscription is established and a no-op function is returned.
If shouldHandleStateChanges is true, subscription.onStateChange is assigned to the update checker, subscription.trySubscribe() is called, and the update checker is run once immediately.
The returned unsubscribe function marks the subscription inactive, calls subscription.tryUnsubscribe(), and clears subscription.onStateChange.
When the selector produces changed child props, the corresponding refs are updated, renderIsScheduled.current becomes true, and additionalSubscribeListener() is called.
When the selector produces the same child props and no render is scheduled, notifyNestedSubs() is called.
invariants: Updates received after unsubscription or while isMounted.current is false are ignored.
At most the most recent selector error is retained for possible propagation during unsubscribe.
A successful selector evaluation clears any previously retained selector error.
Nested subscribers are not notified when a render is already scheduled.
edgeCases: When shouldHandleStateChanges is false, the function returns a no-op unsubscribe callback without accessing the store or subscription.
When isMounted.current is false, an update callback returns without calling store.getState() or the selector.
When childPropsSelector throws, the error is retained, development builds log the error, and no child-prop or render scheduling refs are updated for that evaluation.
When childPropsSelector returns the same reference as lastChildProps.current, child props are not replaced; nested subscribers are notified only if no render is scheduled.
When childPropsSelector returns a different value, that value is stored in both lastChildProps.current and childPropsFromStoreUpdate.current and a render is scheduled.
When unsubscribe is called after an unresolved selector error, that error is thrown after the subscription is detached.

raises: The most recently caught selector error is rethrown by the returned unsubscribe function if no later successful selector evaluation cleared it.
errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Selector exceptions are caught during update processing rather than immediately propagated; other dependency failures are not handled.
errorPolicy.returnsOnError: No update result is returned; a no-op or unsubscribe callback is returned depending on shouldHandleStateChanges.
